title: Armor Marine (SSgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O #
raw_text:
2.     MOS 1812, Armor Marine (SSgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O #

    a. Summary. THIS IS AN OBSOLETE MOS, NO LONGER IN USE IN THE TABLE OF
ORGANIZATION OF THE MARINE CORPS. THIS MOS IS MAINTAINED IN THE MOS MANUAL
BECAUSE IT APPEARS IN THE RECORDS OF MARINES STILL ON ACTIVE DUTY. As
members of an M1A1 tank crew or unit, Armor Marines perform duties necessary
for the proper maintenance, operation, and employment of the M1A1 Main Battle
Tank (MBT). These duties include preparing the tank, personnel, and
supporting equipment to support training and combat operations, preparation
of ammunition, acquiring targets, employment of organic tank weapons
utilizing the fire control system, driving the tank, and conducting operator-
level preventive and corrective maintenance.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must have normal color vision.

            (2) Must have vision correctable to 20/20.

            (3) Must possess a GT score of 90 or higher.

            (4) Must have a WS-B water survival qualification.

        (5) Security clearance requirements:       must be eligible for a secret
clearance.

        (6) Must meet MOS classification standards as listed in the glossary
(pg. xiv) prior to graduating from recruit training.

        (7) Must meet initial strength test standards associated with PEF
assignments as listed in the glossary (pg. xiv) prior to shipping to recruit
training.

    c. Requirements.        Complete the M1A1 Armor Crewmember Course (A03TBM2) at
Ft Moore, GA.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (m), Tank Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Armored Assault Vehicle Crew Members 55-3013.


                                         3-131                        Enclosure (1)
 3119                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

# MOS 1812 is no longer a PMOS for gunnery sergeants through master gunnery
sergeants. When promoted to GySgt, the 1869 PMOS will be awarded after
completing the MOS requirements. To facilitate M&RA with assignments,
Marines may be assigned using the intended MOS (IMOS) for which they were
selected until they have met the requirements.

COMBAT VEHICLE 1. Introduction. The Tank, Assault Amphibious Vehicle and Amphibious Combat Vehicle OccFld includes operation, employment, maneuver, and maintenance of tracked vehicles in the combined arms environment during both amphibious assaults and subsequent land operations ashore. Qualifications required include basic mechanical aptitude and the ability to perform harmoniously with others in the confined area inside combat vehicles. The duties involved are incident to the operation, employment, maneuver, and maintenance of tanks and assault amphibious vehicles. Formal schooling is provided to Marines at both the entry level and at the appropriate time in career development. Marines entering this OccFld receive MOS 1800, Basic Tank and Assault Amphibious Marine. After entry into OccFld 18 and assignment of a basic 1800 MOS, personnel specialize in either the M1A1 Tank or the Assault Amphibious Vehicle are assigned MOS 1812, 1833, or 1834 respectively.

2. MOS 1812, Armor Marine (SSgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O # a. Summary. THIS IS AN OBSOLETE MOS, NO LONGER IN USE IN THE TABLE OF ORGANIZATION OF THE MARINE CORPS. THIS MOS IS MAINTAINED IN THE MOS MANUAL BECAUSE IT APPEARS IN THE RECORDS OF MARINES STILL ON ACTIVE DUTY. As members of an M1A1 tank crew or unit, Armor Marines perform duties necessary for the proper maintenance, operation, and employment of the M1A1 Main Battle Tank (MBT). These duties include preparing the tank, personnel, and supporting equipment to support training and combat operations, preparation of ammunition, acquiring targets, employment of organic tank weapons utilizing the fire control system, driving the tank, and conducting operator- level preventive and corrective maintenance. b. Prerequisites (1) Must have normal color vision. (2) Must have vision correctable to 20/20. (3) Must possess a GT score of 90 or higher. (4) Must have a WS-B water survival qualification. (5) Security clearance requirements: must be eligible for a secret clearance. (6) Must meet MOS classification standards as listed in the glossary (pg. xiv) prior to graduating from recruit training. (7) Must meet initial strength test standards associated with PEF assignments as listed in the glossary (pg. xiv) prior to shipping to recruit training. c. Requirements. Complete the M1A1 Armor Crewmember Course (A03TBM2) at Ft Moore, GA. d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (m), Tank Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
